cells.tense: The pull toward what you actually want is here, and the practice has caught up to it.
cells.act: draw the shape of it without the details
cells.ask: Take a piece of the practice and sketch its shape in a few plain lines — how it holds together — no details, no steps. Look at it, then set it down.
cells.core:
What you want has stopped being a direction you squint toward. The hours alone with the same small thing have turned it into something your hands can do, and you light up in rooms now because there is substance behind the light, not because you announced anything.

There is a way to see the whole of it from above. Take the practice you have been refining and sketch its shape in a few plain lines — what it is, how it moves, what makes it hold — leaving out every detail that usually fills your thinking. You are not improving it or planning the next stage. You are seeing it whole. After that, what to refine next tends to be obvious, and it is rarely the part you expected.
cells.sheetLine: You're not performing it anymore. You're standing on it.
cells.verb: shining because the work reached completion
cells.place: the solitary hours where skill is built by repetition

cells.tense: You will have lit the whole road before you have walked any of it.
cells.act: wait until you know which part matters, then begin with that part
cells.ask: Before you sit down to the work, hold off until the part that matters most today is clear, then begin with just that part. Let the rest wait.
cells.core:
The light runs out past the practice. From outside it reads as confidence — the finished version described before the first one exists, brightness pointed at what comes next while the present sits unattended. From inside it is harder to stay put, and staying put is the job here. People are dazzled by where you are going and cannot quite see where you are.

The correction is quieter than the problem. Before you sit down to the work, hold off until the part that matters most is clear to you, and begin only with that one part. Let everything else wait its turn. You will lose the pleasure of describing the summit for a while. What you get instead is a practice that is actually yours to stand on.
cells.sheetLine: You're describing the finished thing before you've built the first one.

cells.tense: You practised and it never flowered, and you have stopped standing at that door.
cells.act: tend it small and ask nothing of it
cells.ask: Choose the smallest piece of the practice — a few minutes, one repetition — and do just that much, asking nothing of it, no result owed today.
cells.core:
There was a pull toward something once, and it wore down under hours going in with nothing coming out. That is what happened to the practice — not a failure of desire, but a long stretch where desire had nothing to feed on. The hours are still there and the light is not.

Go smaller than you would choose. Take the tiniest piece of it — a few minutes, one repetition, the most basic version — and do that much with nothing riding on it. No result owed today, no measuring whether it is returning. Care that does not demand an outcome is what feeds a thing this starved. If you can do that tomorrow too, do it. Ask nothing else of it.
cells.sheetLine: You kept showing up long after it stopped giving anything back.
cells.verb: shining because the work reached completion

cells.tense: Something you built by repetition is shining on people, and you would say you were not part of it.
cells.act: keep it at its real size when you are asked to shrink it
cells.ask: When someone names the practice as your doing, let it stand at its real size — no deflecting, no shrinking it to seem modest. Say what you did.
cells.core:
The thing you make by doing it again and again is reaching people, and your own account of it has not kept up. You would call it luck, or temperament, or nothing much. Ask the people who lean on what you built and they will not describe luck. They will describe someone who kept at it in the hours nobody saw.

Attention is the cost. When someone names the work as yours, let it stand at its real size — do not shrink it to seem modest, do not wave it off. Say what you actually did, in the plainest sentence you have. That is not bragging; it is accuracy. You may find the light is not something you have been carrying without noticing, but something you have been building, by hand.
cells.sheetLine: You've been shining and calling it nothing much.
cells.verb: shining because the work reached completion
